newsitem.title: POLAND: EARLY ZLOTY JUMPS AS C.BANK HINTS MORE TIGHTENING.
newsitem.headline: EARLY ZLOTY JUMPS AS C.BANK HINTS MORE TIGHTENING.

text.p: The zloty quickly gained about half a percentage point in early Monday trade as Polish banks bought zlotys after the central bank said that it may have to further tighten its monetary policy, dealers said.
"The zloty rose on news from the National Bank of Poland (NBP). It may still firm further toward parity later today," said Jerzy Wyjadlowski, forex dealer at Bank Slaski SA.

In a Saturday newspaper a senior NBP official said the bank may again tighten its monetary policy because commercial banks were not sufficiently raising credit and deposit rates after last week's official interest rate increase.

Polish T-bill yields were expected to rise at Monday's 1.1 billion zloty tender after the Treasury let T-bond yields rise last week, but even this may not lure larger foreign capital back into Polish paper ahead of next month's elections.
Dealers said that T-bill yields should rise between 10 and 35 basis points at Monday's primary tender, with demand focused on shorter eight and 13-week bills.

"We are still waiting for the reaction of (the state savings bank) PKO BP, but basically we already know that the hitherto (rate) increases in commercial banks are too small," the Rzeczpospolita daily quoted monetary policy head Jerzy Stopyra as saying.
"We may use other (monetary policy) instruments," he said.
At 0805 GMT the zloty was at -0.28/-0.35 percent from the central parity rate, up from opening's -0.71/-0.88 percent.
It was at 3.4680/00 to the dollar against 3.4770/20 at opening and at 1.8700/15 to the mark against 1.8820/60.
On August 4 the NBP increased its lombard rate by two points to 27 percent and discount by 2.5 to 24.5 percent.
Stopyra said that as a result of the official rate rise commercial banks increased credit rates by 1.0-1.5 points but that they barely changed their deposit rates.

On the money market overnight rates eased a fraction to 22.80/23.05 percent from opening's 22.90/23.10 percent and tomorrow/next to 22.90/23.15 percent from 22.95/23.15 percent, aparently not effected by the central bank's warning.
Dealers expected the that in the longer term rates may rise but that a cash surplus presently dominated the market.
